Rashi on Ketubot 61a:10:1.english: Except for pouring a cup - Anything that involves matters of closeness and affection, and leads to familiarity with the matter [of intimacy].

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:11:1.english: She would change [her practice] for him - [That is,] during the days of her whiteness [her clean days prior to immersion].

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:12:1.hebrew: הכל משהין לפני שמש - המשמש בסעודה, ואוכלין בפניו, ושוהין מלהאכילו עד שיקומו הקרואים:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:12:1.english: All [foods] may be withheld before a waiter - [One] who serves at a meal, and they eat in front of him, and they delay feeding him until the invited guests arise.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:12:2.english: Except for fatty meat, etc. - For he craves them and is distressed.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:12:3.english: During the season of Tammuz - For its aroma is strong, and the heat of the day burns within him like venom.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:1.english: A cooked dish of ardei - A type of truffles and mushrooms.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:2.english: I would have been endangered - I was in danger of being seized by bulmus [faintness from hunger] because of the craving of my hunger.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:3.hebrew: גרגלידי - חתיכות דקות ועגולות, מריר"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:3.english: Gargelidei - Thin, round slices, merira in Old French.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:4.hebrew: תמרתא דהנוניתא - תמרה שמינה, כמו: "קריב לגבי דהינא ואידהן" (שבועות דף מז:):
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:4.english: Tamarta dehanunita - A fatty date, like [the saying,] "Draw near to the fatty one and become fatty" (Shevuot 47b).

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:5.hebrew: קיוהא - קיהיון שיניים, איגרו"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:5.english: Kiyuha - Setting the teeth on edge [i.e., tartness], aigror in Old French.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:13:6.english: Anything that has an aroma or a sharp taste - [It] harms one before whom they eat [it] and he does not eat [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:14:1.english: One [of them] feeds - [He] feeds the attendant from every single kind.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:14:2.hebrew: וחד ספי ליה ממין אחד - בתחלת סעודה לשובע, ומשאר המינין משההו עד שיגמור סעודתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:14:2.english: And one would feed him from one type - at the beginning of the meal to satiety, and [as for] the other types, he keeps him waiting until he finishes his meal.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:15:1.english: Would feed [him] earlier - Before [the attendant] places [food] before him.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:15:2.hebrew: מאחר ספי - מכל מין ומין, לאחר שנתן לפניו ולפני האורחין:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:15:2.english: Feeds [him] afterwards - [He gives the waiter] from every kind [of food], after he has placed [it] before himself and before the guests.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:15:3.hebrew: דקדים ספי משתעי אליהו בהדיה - לפי שכשנותן לפניהן, והוא רואה ומתאוה ומצטער, ופעמים שיש אורחין הרבה:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:15:3.english: The one who feeds [the waiter] earlier, Elijah spoke with him - Because when he places [the food] before them [the guests], he [the waiter] sees [it] and craves [it] and is distressed, and sometimes there are many guests.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:16:1.english: Izgur - [The] name of a king of Persia.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:16:2.hebrew: אטורנגא דמלכא - מושיב המנות לפני השרים, ובלשונינו שינישקלאקו"ש:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:16:2.english: The king's aturanga - [The one who] sets the portions before the nobles, and in our language [Old French], seneschal.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:2:1.english: It is her pain - The milk is abundant in her breasts and causes her pain.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:2:2.english: That it is not her custom - It is not the custom of her family to nurse.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:4:1.hebrew: בחריקאי - במקומי. ולי נראה לשון חידקי קרן, כלומר לשון פקידת מקום, בפקד מקומי ובפגמי:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:4:1.english: Baḥarikai - In my place. But it appears to me [that it is] an expression of notches of a horn, that is to say, an expression of a vacant place — in the vacancy of my place and in my gap [of absence].

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:5:1.english: Guests - Guests who stay [for] a week or a month.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:5:2.hebrew: פרחי - עוברים לדרכם, לפי שבמקום שיש בני בית רבים, נוהגים להתארח עוברי דרך:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:5:2.english: Wayfarers - Passersby on their way, because in a place where there are many household members, travelers are accustomed to lodge [there].

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:6:1.english: But the other [tasks] - Such as small matters.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:8:1.hebrew: שראויה להכניס - שהכניסה נדוניא רבה, ויש כדאי למביאה נדוניא זו לקנות ממקצתה שפחות להכניס ולשמשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:8:1.english: That she is able to bring [maidservants] - [This means] that she brought in a large dowry, and she who brings this dowry has enough to buy maidservants with part of it to bring [in] and serve her.

Rashi on Ketubot 61a:9:1.hebrew: אבל מוזגת לו כוס ומצעת לו מטה - לפרוס סדין ולבדין, דבר שאינו טורח, ומשום דמילי דחיבה נינהו, כדי שתתחבב עליו. ולא דמי למצעת דמתני', דהוי דבר של טורח ובכפייה; הני לא כפי לה, אלא חכמים השיאוה עצה טובה להנהיג זאת בישראל:
Rashi on Ketubot 61a:9:1.english: However, she pours his cup and makes a bed for him - [Meaning] to spread a sheet and felt blankets, something that is not burdensome, and [she does so] because they are matters of affection, so that she will endear herself to him. And it is not similar to "making the bed" [mentioned] in the Mishnah, which is a burdensome matter and [enforced] by compulsion; [regarding] these, they do not compel her, rather the Sages gave her good advice to practice this in Israel.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:11:1.hebrew: מחלפא דביתהו בידא דשמאלא - במחזור ויטרי פי' הרב ר' שמעיה, שהיה נזהר רש"י אפי' שלא ליתן מפתח מידו לידה. ומכאן אין ראיה, דשאני מזיגת כוס שהוא דבר של חיבה, ואסורה אפילו להביא לפניו על השולחן, אלא למר מנחא ליה אבי סדיא, ולמר אפומא דכובא. ומסדר אליהו, דקתני גבי ההוא עובדא דמייתי בפ"ק דשבת (דף יג: ושם) באדם אחד שקרא הרבה ושנה הרבה כו', ששאל אליהו לאשתו: "שמא הבאת לו את הפך, שמא הבאת לו את השמן?" ואמרה לו: "חס ושלום, אפי' באצבע קטנה לא נגע בי!" — נמי אין ראיה, דמצינן לפרש דשלא על הבאת הפך היה מקפיד, אלא הכי קאמר: "שמא בשעת הבאת הפך לא נזהרת ונגע ביך?" וכן משמע, שהשיבתו: "אפילו באצבע קטנה לא נגע בי", אבל שלא הביאה לו לא קאמרה. ומה שפירש רש"י דמחלפא ליה בידא דשמאלא בימי לבונה, דמשמע שיש להקל בימי לבונה מבימי נדותה — וכן מצינו בפרק קמא דשבת (שם) בההוא עובדא שהבאתי לעיל, דקאמר: "בימי נדותיך מהו אצלך? בימי לבוניך מהו אצלך?" — נראה דהיו רגילין לטבול אחר שבעה לראיה כשפוסקת, דלא אסירא השתא אלא מדרבנן; אבל בזמן הזה, שאין רגילות לטבול עד אחר שבעה נקיים, אין חילוק בין ימי נדות לימי לבון, כדאמרינן במסכת שבת (דף סד:): "תהיה בנדתה" — בהווייתה תהא עד שתבא במים:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:11:1.english: His wife would change [her practice] with her left hand - In Machzor Vitry, HaRav Rabbi Shemayah explained that Rashi was careful not even to pass a key from his hand to her hand. And from here there is no proof [to the contrary], for pouring a cup is different, as it is an act of affection, and she is forbidden even to bring [it] before him onto the table; rather, for one [Amora] she would place it on his pillow, and for another, on top of a barrel. And from Seder Eliyahu, which teaches regarding that incident cited in the first chapter of Shabbat (13b and ibid.), about a certain man who had read much [Scripture] and studied much [Mishnah], etc., where Eliyahu asked his wife: "Perhaps you brought him the flask? Perhaps you brought him the oil?" and she said to him: "Heaven forbid! He did not touch me even with a little finger!" — there is also no proof [that handing an object is forbidden], for we can explain that it was not about bringing the flask that he was particular, but rather this is what he meant: "Perhaps while bringing the flask you were not careful and he touched you?" And so it appears, since she answered him: "He did not touch me even with a little finger," whereas she did not say that she had not brought [it] to him. And as for what [Rashi] explained, that "she would change for him with her left hand" [refers to] during her white days — which implies that one may be more lenient during her white days than during the days of her niddah [flow] — and similarly we find in the first chapter of Shabbat (ibid.) in that incident I cited above, where [Eliyahu] said: "During the days of your niddah [flow], how was he with you? During your white days, how was he with you?" — it appears that they were accustomed to immerse [in a mikveh] after seven [days] from the sighting [of blood] once it ceased, so that she was now only forbidden by rabbinic decree; however, nowadays, when it is not the practice to immerse until after seven clean [days], there is no distinction between the days of niddah and the white days, as we say in Tractate Shabbat (64b): "She shall be in her niddah [state]" — she shall remain in her status until she enters the water.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:4:1.hebrew: הכניסה לו שפחה אחת - קצת תימה: אם הוא זן אותה, א"כ מה מרויח הבעל? דבלא שפחה היא היתה עושה הכל ולא היה זן אלא אותה לבדה, ועתה זן אותה ואת שפחתה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:4:1.english: If she brought him one maidservant - It is somewhat puzzling: if he feeds [the maidservant], if so, what does the husband gain? For without a maidservant, she [the wife] would do everything, and he would only feed her alone, whereas now he feeds her and her maidservant.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:6:1.hebrew: יכול יהא חלב מהלכי שתים טמא ודם מהלכי שתים טמא - בת"כ גרסי' "בשר" במקום "דם", וקאמר: ת"ל "זה" — אוציא חלב שאינו נוהג בכל, פירוש: דחלב בהמה טהורה מותר, ולא אוציא את הבשר שהוא נוהג בכל, שאף בבהמה טהורה אסור בשר מן החי? ת"ל "זה טמא" — זה בלא תעשה על אכילתו, ואין בשר מהלכי שתים כו'. ואור"י, דבין לפי ספרים שלנו דדריש מ"הוא" היתר חלב ודם, ובין לת"כ דדריש מ"זה", אתי שפיר, דמצי למעוטי חלב, בשר, ודם כולהו מחד קרא, כמו שמצינו בכמה מקומות דממעטין מחד קרא כמה דברים, כדאשכחן בפרק הנהנה מן ההקדש (מעילה יח:) דכמה פעמים קאמר "תמעול מעל" — ריבה. ופליגא השתא אברייתא דפרק דם שחיטה (כריתות כ: ושם), דממעט דם מהלכי שתים מדכתיב "לעוף ולבהמה". ויש ספרים דממעטין חלב מדכתיב "הוא" ודם מדכתיב "זה". ותימה לר"י: דמנא לן לאוקמא אדם? דסברא הוא יותר לאוקמא אבשר ולהתיר בשר מדם, דאין איסור בשר נוהג בכל אלא מחיים, אבל דם — איסורו נוהג בכל, בין מחיים בין לאחר מיתה. ואור"י, דאי הוה גריס בשמעתין "בשר" במקום "דם", הוה אתי שפיר: דמ"זה" ומ"הוא" ממעטינן חלב ובשר, ומההוא קרא דכריתות ממעטינן דם. וא"ת: וכיון דממעטינן דם מההוא קרא דכריתות, אמאי איצטריך קרא למישרי חלב? השתא דם מותר, חלב לא כ"ש? וי"ל, דמההוא קרא דכריתות לא מצי למישרי דם לגמרי, דלא ממעטינן ליה אלא מאיסור דם, אבל מאיסור טמא לא ממעטינן ליה; והואיל ונתמעט מאיסור דם, השתא דם וחלב שוין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:6:1.english: "One might think that the milk of bipeds is impure, and the blood of bipeds is impure" - In Torat Kohanim, we read "flesh" in place of "blood," and it states: "The verse states, 'this' — [meaning] I will exclude milk, which does not apply in all cases, explanation: for the milk of a kosher animal is permitted, and shall I not exclude flesh, which applies in all cases, for even in a kosher animal, flesh from a living [animal] is forbidden? The verse states, 'this is impure' — this [non-kosher animal] is subject to a negative commandment against eating it, whereas the flesh of bipeds [is not], etc." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that both according to our texts, which derive the permission of milk and blood from "hu" ["it"], and according to Torat Kohanim, which derives [it] from "zeh" ["this"], it works out well, for it can exclude milk, flesh, and blood — all of them — from a single verse, just as we find in several places that we exclude several things from a single verse, as we find in the chapter HaNeheneh Min HaHekdesh (Me'ilah 18b), where several times it says: "'Tim'ol ma'al' ['commit a trespass'] is an inclusion." And this now disagrees with the baraita in the chapter Dam Shechitah (Keritot 20b and there [in the parallel]), which excludes the blood of bipeds from what is written, "for fowl and for beast." And there are texts that exclude milk from what is written "hu" and blood from what is written "zeh." And this is surprising to Rabbeinu Yitzchak: From where do we know to apply [one of them] to blood? For it is more logical to apply it to flesh and to permit flesh rather than blood, since the prohibition of flesh does not apply in all cases, [applying] only during [the animal's] lifetime, whereas blood — its prohibition applies in all cases, both during [its] lifetime and after death. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that if [the text] in our passage were to read "flesh" in place of "blood," it would work out well: for from "zeh" and from "hu" we would exclude milk and flesh, and from that verse in Keritot we would exclude blood. And if you ask: Since we exclude blood from that verse in Keritot, why is a verse needed to permit milk? Now [that] blood is permitted, [is] milk not all the more so [permitted]? And one can answer: From that verse in Keritot, it cannot permit blood completely, for we only exclude it from the prohibition of blood, but from the prohibition of an impure [creature] we do not exclude it; and once it has been excluded from the prohibition of blood, now blood and milk are equal.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:8:1.hebrew: ואחת שצמצמה לו משלה גרסי' - פירוש: צמצמה לו ממה שהוא חייב ליתן לה, כמו קופה של בשמים ושאר דברים, וצמצמה כל כך שיכול לקנות מזה כמה שפחות — רבינו תם. ויש גורסין: "שמצאה לו משלו", כלומר שהוא עשיר שיכול לקנות הרבה שפחות כפי צרכה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:8:1.english: "And one [case] where she reduced [her needs] for him from hers" is our reading - Explanation: she reduced [her demands] for him from what he is obligated to give her, such as a basket of spices and other things, and she reduced [them] so much that he can buy several maidservants from this — [so explains] Rabbeinu Tam. And there are those who read [the text as]: "that she found for him from his," meaning that he is wealthy, such that he can buy many maidservants according to her needs.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:9:1.hebrew: אבל מוזגת לו את הכוס ומצעת לו המטה - והא דתנן: "שלש אינה מצעת", כתבתי בריש מכילתין (דף ד:) [דלא הוי כמו הצעת המטה דמתני']:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61a:9:1.english: But she pours the cup for him and makes the bed for him - And [regarding] that which we learned [in the Mishnah]: "[If she brought] three [maidservants], she does not make [the bed]," I have [already] written at the beginning of our tractate (4b) [that this is not like the making of the bed in the Mishnah].
